The Flood Watch for Travis County expires at 7 PM CDT tonight — flooding risk remains active through this evening but conditions are improving. Downtown Austin's active hit-and-run homicide investigation (I-35 service road, Friday night) keeps Physical Security ELEVATED; suspect vehicle remains at large. incidents.title: Flood Watch — Travis County (EXPIRES 7 PM CDT Today)
incidents.detail: NWS Austin/San Antonio Flood Watch remains in effect for Travis County through 7 PM CDT Tuesday. Frontal boundary has stalled just west of I-35 with abundant tropical moisture persisting (PWAT 2.0–2.4 in). Rain chance 50% Tuesday with residual heavy cells possible (2–3 in/hr). Soils fully saturated — any additional rainfall will run off rapidly. Flood Watch expires tonight; conditions expected to dry out Wednesday. Shoal Creek (W) and Waller Creek (E) remain at elevated stage; monitor water levels before restoring outdoor operations. Do NOT restore valet on flood-prone approach roads until Flood Watch officially expires and roads are confirmed passable.

incidents.title: Hit-and-Run Homicide — I-35 Service Road (Active APD Investigation)
incidents.location: 600 blk N. I-35 Southbound Service Road (~0.4 mi E)
incidents.detail: APD Vehicular Homicide Unit is investigating a fatal hit-and-run that occurred approximately 11:35 PM Friday, June 13. A male pedestrian was struck on the N. I-35 southbound service road at 600 block and died at the hospital. Suspect vehicle: 2011–2015 gray or silver Hyundai Sonata with front-end damage and missing right headlight — at large as of 0500 CDT June 16. No arrest made. This is approximately 0.4 mi east of the property. Advise valet and staff: report any sightings of matching vehicle to APD non-emergency (512) 974-5000. Brief guest-facing staff on the active investigation if guests ask about I-35 corridor activity.

incidents.title: U.S.–Iran MOU Electronically Signed — Framework Framework Deal
incidents.detail: President Trump confirmed Monday evening the U.S.–Iran MOU has been electronically signed by Trump, VP Vance, and Iranian Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf. The MOU (~1.5 pages) is a general framework: 60-day ceasefire extension, Strait of Hormuz toll-free reopening, IAEA nuclear inspectors to return, Iran to assist in destruction of highly enriched uranium stockpile. Formal signing ceremony: Friday, June 19, Geneva (Vance attending; Trump may also attend). Significant details disputed: Iran claims $12B frozen asset release required; Vance denies any sanctions relief without performance. Strait of Hormuz expected to be fully operational Friday. Austin relevance: Iranian cyber retaliation risk declining but NOT cleared until Hormuz formally reopens June 19. Maintain zero-click, zero-QR posture for guest-facing staff through Friday. WC-themed phishing remains active (10,000+ malicious domains).
